newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Van Miert sees no quick decision on BA/AMR pact.
newsitem.headline: Van Miert sees no quick decision on BA/AMR pact.

text.p: European Competition Commissioner Karel Van Miert said on Tuesday that the Commission was unlikely to rule on the alliance between British Airways and American Airlines before the end of August.
"This is certainly going beyond the summer break," Van Miert told reporters as he arrived for a conference organised by the Wall Street Journal Europe.
Replying to questions about a meeting on Monday with BA chairman Robert Ayling, Van Miert said the talks had been constructive.

But because the Commission would have to consult a committee of national competition officials twice on the alliance, a final recommendation was unlikely to be adopted before the Commission broke for its summer recess in August.

He said that under a rarely-used procedure covering alliances between EU and non-EU carriers, a first meeting of the advisory committee would have to be called, but in the meantime the Commission would continue discussing with the parties how to address the competition concerns posed by the deal.
"Once you have a solution, you have to go back to the consultative committee," Van Miert said.

Van Miert's comments scotched the belief expressed by senior EU officials and antitrust lawyers recently that the Commission would be able to reach a final position on the controversial alliance before the end of July.

The Commission is investigating the case under article 89 of the EU treaty in close co-operation with the British government which will take the final decision on whether the deal respects treaty provisions banning agreements restricting competition and abuse of dominant position.

Van Miert has openly criticised a preliminary ruling by Britain's Office of Fair Trading in December that BA and American release 168 weekly take-off and landing slots at London Heathrow -- enough to operate 12 daily return flights -- to make room for competitors.

While British Airways called the figure excessive, rival airlines and the European Commission have said more concessions were needed if BA and American were to be prevented from dominating the Anglo-U.S. route.
